note: The matrix is models, not vendors. `candidate` rows are ones that could ship and are what the gate acts on; `ceiling` rows exist only to answer whether there is headroom worth chasing, and never fail a build. Costs are per million tokens, for the report — a request is roughly 2k in and 400 out, so a month at four photos a day is about 120 requests. `control` rows are kept only to prove a check works and never gate anything: qwen fabricates a nutrition panel on almost every dish — 623 wrong figures against 5 for every other model, including 420 calories for a tray of whole fruit — so it is the row that shows the invented-panel gate has teeth.

models.why: Recall 89% and structure 84%, so it sees the food. Disqualified on fabrication, not vision: 2/46 with 623 invented panel figures on 2026-08-06. Pinned to the dated snapshot (free quota) rather than the rolling alias, which also keeps the control row's answers stable.

Production from 2026-08-15, and taken on price rather than on accuracy — say so plainly. Against 3.6-flash over three runs of both golden cases it was not better on the figure a person sees: bibimbap energy -22/-12/-19% against a published 670 kcal where 3.6 gave -14/-28/-16%. It reads about 48% more grams at a correspondingly lower density — 640 g of bibimbap at ~85 kcal/100 g, where the board's own figure is 156 — so both the weight and the composition move, and it still lands short. What it does win is stability: 442/442/447 g on the pasta where 3.6 gave 292/472/302, and weight variance is the documented open problem. Two cases cannot settle that either way. The price is introductory: $0.75/$3.75 through 2026-12-31, then $1.50/$7.50, which is exactly what 3.6 cost. Revisit before January, by which time the golden set should be big enough to decide on merit.

Production until 2026-08-15 and kept as the row 3.7-flash has to beat. Reads the more plausible density and the less plausible quantity: 340-360 g of a 430 g bibimbap at about the right kcal/100 g. Its weakness is spread, not bias.

Reasoning model on Meta's Responses API, so it takes the same strict json_schema Luna does. Priced under gemini-3.6-flash on both sides, but it is a reasoning model billing its thinking as output — judge it on cost per photo rather than on the rate card. The `-contributor` snapshot is a fifth of the price and deliberately not used: Meta may train on what is sent to it, and these are photographs of someone's dinner.
